reviews.review:
As my first game played in the Warhammer 40,000 universe, I've enjoyed it mostly and the best comparison would be Gears of War clone. Granted, both games are similar but at least on GoW, the game mechanics works better.

In Space Marine, the mechanics aren't that solid. You can't properly cover and shoot. The weapons lack in variety.

The action is satisfying to say the least. The melee *pwning* is quite enjoyable!

Sadly, the campaign mode is very short and VERY LINEAR. There's no exploration to be had. Story is average too. Voice acting is weak. 

My biggest complain would be the poor level design that stops you from moving properly. There's always ground occlusions that blocks you around and you get hit on every sides by that unfortunate event. The controls are semi-responsive.

I barely tried the online mode but I don't like it so far and will skip the rest.


[h1]RECOMMENDATION:[/h1]
Do I recommend? Hardcore WH40K fan or not, it's a fun game regardless so yes, give this fun game a shot!

This is a really fun third person shooter. You kill massive amounts of enemies. Full of blood and gore. Not super challenging but you will probably die a few times. The online multiplayer is not great but is still fun. It is a short game, which is good, because the game ends a long time before you get bored with the mechanics. 

Boss fight was a bit anticlimactic. The exceptional voice acting and game-rendered cutscenes keep you immersed.

Here we have violence. But it's not just regular violence, nonono! It's EPIC violence. This is the violence and grim-darkness that is supposed to permeate the Warhammer universe-- and every Bolter round makes a satisfying sound when it connects with an Ork's skull. That you regain health by execution moves should speak volumes about what to expect. Expect fountains of blood, but also expect a fairly fun third-person hack-and-slash-and-shoot-and-explode-into-kibbles-and-bits game. The squeamish need not apply.

Also, jetpacks. For. The. Win.

After an hour of playing, I was severely disappointed. In the game, in the 40K universe, in everything. This was my introduction after having friends nag me to play Dark Heresy with them for the past few months, and me always making hasty assumptions on the Warhammer 40K uni based on the stereotyping inherent in this game's very title that made me cringe. It doesn't help that I'm no fan of hack 'n' slash.

As I continued to play, however, I found myself sucked back in again and again, thinking of this game in my off-hours, and suddenly the depth to the game's world and gameplay and the flat-looking characters started showing through, and gosh dang, I'm now seeing what keeps my hombres so enthralled in this self-consciously macho 'n' manly Warhammer business. These MFin' space marines are Zen, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's a fun diversion, this game, and the story, while predictable, was pretty well-done and -paced--for the most part (the Ork waves did get a tad exhausting).

Ever wanted to feel what it's like to murder thousands of rampant green skins with nothing but your fury as your sword and faith as your shield....

Apply here.
